summary: The MCP HTTP transport lets one JSON-RPC tools/call body run to a maximum supported upload (base64 of 100 MiB plus 4096 slack, plus a 4 MiB envelope); every other request keeps the 4 MiB bound.
reason: The MCP tools accept a multipart file of up to 100 MiB as base64 (about 134 MiB of text), but the generated HTTP wrapper capped every request body at 4 MiB, so any upload over about 3 MiB was refused 413 before reaching the tool (Greptile PR #2450 thread 4514749152, P1). Scoping the larger cap to a single tools/call keeps initialize, tools/list, notifications and batches at 4 MiB.
validated_outcome: TestNovel1219MCPHTTPMaxSupportedUploadPasses (a tools/call carrying base64 of 100 MiB passes the production limits; red on the 4 MiB cap), TestNovel1219MCPHTTPToolCallCapCoversMaxUpload, TestNovel1219MCPHTTPNonToolCallKeepsTheGeneralBound (tools/list at 4 MiB + 1 is 413), TestNovel1219MCPHTTPBodyLimitEdges (tools/call at and one over its cap; tools/list at and one over the general cap; initialize, batch and malformed bodies over the general cap refused) and TestMCPHTTPDeclaredOversizeBodyIsRefused (declared length one over the tools/call cap refused before any read).
